ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Place two identical wooden blocks A and B, each with a mass of 4 kg, on a horizontal table. Under the action of a horizontal pulling force $F_1$ of 16 N, blocks A and B move together in uniform linear motion. (Take $g = 10\mathrm{N/kg}$)

1. At this moment, what is the magnitude of the frictional force $F_{f1}$ on the upper surface of block B?
2. What is the frictional force $F_{f2}$ on the lower surface of B?
3. What is the coefficient of kinetic friction between the tabletop and the wooden block?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Place two identical wooden blocks A and B, each with a mass of 4 kg, on a horizontal table. Under the action of a horizontal pulling force $F_1$ of 16 N, blocks A and B move together in uniform linear motion. (Take $g = 10\mathrm{N/kg}$) 1. At this moment, what is the magnitude of the frictional force $F_{f1}$ on the upper surface of block B? 2. What is the frictional force $F_{f2}$ on the lower surface of B? 3. What is the coefficient of kinetic friction between the tabletop and the wooden block?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, wooden block A is stacked above wooden block B, and B is placed on a horizontal tabletop; on the right side of B there is a horizontal rightward pulling force F1, whose magnitude is given by the problem as 16 N; A and B together undergo uniform linear motion. Reasoning: First analyze the upper wooden block A alone. A has no externally applied pulling force in the horizontal direction, and the only force it may receive in the horizontal direction is the friction force exerted by B on A. Since A and B move uniformly together, the acceleration is 0, so the resultant force on A in the horizontal direction is 0; therefore the friction force on the contact surface between A and B must be 0. From action and reaction, it can be known that the friction force Ff1 received by the upper surface of B is also 0. Then regard A and B as a whole. The only external forces in the horizontal direction on the whole are the rightward pulling force F1=16 N and the friction force Ff2 exerted by the tabletop on B. The whole moves uniformly, and the acceleration is 0, so the resultant force in the horizontal direction is 0; therefore the magnitude of the friction force exerted by the tabletop on B is Ff2=16 N, directed to the left. Finally find the coefficient of kinetic friction between the tabletop and the wooden block. The support force exerted by the tabletop on B equals the total weight of A and B: N=(mA+mB)g=(4+4)×10=80 N. From Ff2=μN, get μ=16/80=0.2.
